focus.title: Trail hip load and hold
aimFor: Your trail knee keeps its flex going back
Your hips turn in place going back

rightNow.text: Your trail leg straightens going back
Your hips sway away from the target going back

focus.why: A straight trail leg lets your hips slide instead of turn, so you lose power. When your hips slide away, the bottom of your swing moves and contact gets harder to repeat.
focus.practise: Take your address position, make a slow backswing turn, and stop at the top. Feel the pressure in the trail hip socket rather than on the outside of the trail foot. Hold for three seconds, then return.
focus.reason: Picked first: it comes earliest in your swing and covers two of the things on your list.
